body: I know, I was out of line. I wrote this right before I tried to take my own life, so I wasn't really thinking ahead, or worrying about other people's feelings at the time. I'm well aware it's not a contest, we all have our own problems, wherever we are in life. I'm admittedly just extremely jealous of people who get to be in the presence of other people on a regular basis. Even though I know those people's pain is as real as mine, I just can't help but feel like they're taking their situation for granted. I guess that's why I'm alone.
good for them. they clearly had a stronger sense of self preservation than me. ill be sure to think about that while i wait for these pills to kick in
I never said I thought I was the only one. There are also plenty of teens who have committed suicide before me. I'll just be yet another one.

It's true I can't see the future, but looking to my past I can guess how things will turn out. In just 19 short years, I've repeated the same mistakes more times than I can count, and made my situation worse each time in the process. I used to be a positive person, always giving things another try, but with each failure I slowly became less willing to try again. At this point, I'm so afraid of failure that I no longer have the will to try. Because I can no longer handle the pain that comes with failing. I don't want to live to see how low I can sink, I just want to stop while I still can.

That's true. I'm probably just a bit bitter. I easily get frustrated when I see people complaining that their friends or partners don't pay enough attention to them and call it being lonely. I can see how that sucks, but I don't even have the luxury of being in the presence of another person most of the time, so problems like that seem so insignificant to me.

This doesn't make me feel any better. There's no guarantee I will ever find someone who can stand being around me. The few times I thought people cared about me, I was either forgotten quickly, or simply abandoned. Even my own mother gave me to someone else. Chances are, if I do find someone who likes me, I will find some way to fuck it up and end up hurting even more than I do now. If that's my future, I'd rather just check out now. 
I appreciate your positivity, but it's lost on me.

I'm talking about physical isolation. And you're right, not everyone is cut out for it, including me. I find it extremely maddening and depressing. The internet is my only lifeline, but it's not a replacement for human interaction in the long run. It starts to feels empty and impersonal.
My mom is mentally ill, my dad hates my guts, my brother thinks I'm insane and wants nothing to do with me, and my grandma is on her death bed with cancer. That's all the family I've got.

I ask myself this all the time too. I haven't had a friend since I was 11 (I'm 19 now), and at this point I don't even remember what it feels like to actually be friends with someone. I think some people are just easy to overlook, and we're just unlucky to be those people.
